item.title: CISA Adds Four Known Exploited Vulnerabilities to Catalog
item.description:
CISA has added four new vulnerabilities to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog, based on evidence of active exploitation.

  • CVE-2025-42884 SAP NetWeaver Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in Data Query Logic Vulnerability
  • CVE-2026-76466 Cisco Expressway Series Use of Hard-coded Credentials Vulnerability
  • CVE-2026-123890 VMWare vCenter Authentication Bypass Using an Alternate Path or Channel Vulnerability
  • CVE-2026-129448 Apache Roller Deserialization of Untrusted Data Vulnerability

These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise. 

Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied. 

While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities. CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria. 

Aware of an exploited vulnerability not currently listed in the KEV Catalog? Submit it for potential addition through CISA’s KEV Nomination Form. Potential KEV additions must have a CVE ID, evidence of exploitation, and clear mitigation guidance.

item.title: It’s Time to Settle With Russia
item.description: In October, U.S. President Donald Trump sold his eleventh-hour deal to secure diesel from Russian President Vladimir Putin—pausing sanctions that his own administration had imposed—as a boon for the negotiations to end the war in Ukraine. The arrangement, he wrote on Truth Social, was intended to keep Russia at “the bargaining table.” Of course, it was always obvious to observers that the gambit had as much or more to do with bolstering the U.S. economy and stemming a massive victory for the Democrats in this month’s midterm elections, and in that, it failed.Cynics have grounds for questioning all of Trump’s moves when it comes to Russia and Ukraine. He clearly dislikes Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky and shows a marked preference for illiberal leaders, especially those willing to give him easy wins. Still, a stopped clock can be right twice a day. And concessions such as the fuel deal are exactly what might move Russia and Ukraine closer to peace, even if they are not wholly motivated by public-spiritedness.

item.title: AutomationDirect C-More EA9 Programming Software
item.description:
View CSAF

Summary

Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow attackers to corrupt application memory and cause instability or a crash, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution, if a user is convinced to open a malicious file.

The following versions of AutomationDirect C-More EA9 Programming Software are affected:

  • C-More EA9 Programming Software <=V6.80 (CVE-2026-127280)
CVSS Vendor Equipment
v3 7.8 AutomationDirect C-More EA9 Programming Software
1 Vulnerability
Heap-based Buffer Overflow

Background

  • Critical Infrastructure Sectors: Critical Manufacturing, Energy, Water and Wastewater Systems
  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: United States

Vulnerabilities

CVE-2026-127280
C-More EA9 Programming Software V6.80 does not adequately validate data read from a project file before using it in heap memory operations. A crafted file causes a heap buffer overrun during file open, resulting in heap corruption and instability within the application. An attacker can exploit this vulnerability by convincing a user to open a malicious project file delivered through common distribution channels such as email, file sharing, or removable media.
Read More

1 Affected Product

AutomationDirect C-More EA9 Programming Software <=V6.80

Product Status: known_affected

Remediations

Vendor fix
Update C-More EA9 Programming Software to V6.81: https://www.automationdirect.com/support/software-downloads

Mitigation
If you cannot update to the latest software or firmware version right away, apply the following compensating controls to reduce risk until the update can be performed. These measures are temporary and do not replace the update, which remains the primary and recommended remediation. Apply these controls as appropriate based on the vulnerability, assessed risk, operational requirements, and characteristics of your environment. Implement changes under your established management-of-change process. Before implementing isolation, access-control, or network-configuration changes, evaluate potential impacts to safety, availability, and essential operational functions. • Isolate affected engineering workstations and OT systems from external and nonessential networks, including the internet and corporate IT networks, where operationally feasible. • Disable or tightly restrict vendor, contractor, and other remote access to the affected OT environment until the vulnerability can be remediated. Where remote access is operationally required, use a hardened jump host, enforce multi-factor authentication, apply least-privilege access, and limit access to authorized, time-bound sessions. • Use trusted, dedicated OT networks for device communication. Where practicable and appropriate to the assessed risk, use dedicated or physically separated infrastructure for higher-criticality systems. Where logical segmentation is used, ensure segmentation controls are appropriately configured, secured, and monitored. • Restrict both physical and logical access to affected systems to authorized personnel only. Apply least-privilege principles to administrative, engineering, maintenance, and service access. • Configure application allowlisting, where supported, so that only trusted and pre-approved applications are permitted to execute. Block unauthorized software. • Use appropriate antivirus or endpoint detection and response (EDR) tools where supported and compatible with the affected system. Configure host-based and network firewalls to permit only required communications. • Disable unnecessary services, ports, protocols, and communication pathways associated with the affected systems. Where a service or protocol cannot be disabled for operational reasons, restrict access to trusted systems and authorized users wherever possible. • Enable and regularly review available system, security, and network logs to identify suspicious or unauthorized activity. Where appropriate, monitor communications to and from affected systems for unexpected connections or changes in network behavior. • Maintain secure, tested, and preferably offline backups of PLC programs, device configurations, engineering workstation configurations, and other information necessary to restore operations. Periodically verify that backups can be successfully restored. • Verify that critical OT functions can continue operating without unnecessary dependencies on external networks, cloud services, remote-access services, corporate IT services, or other nonessential systems. • If removable media is required to transfer files into an isolated or restricted environment, use controlled and trusted media and scan it for malicious content before use. • Continuously evaluate the risks associated with operating vulnerable or outdated firmware or software. Adjust compensating controls as the threat environment, operational requirements, or available vulnerability information changes. These compensating controls are intended to reduce exposure while remediation is pending. Organizations should prioritize applying the vendor-provided update as soon as it can be safely tested and deployed within the operational environment.

CISA recommends users take defensive measures to minimize the risk of exploitation of these vulnerabilities.

  • Minimize network exposure for all control system devices and/or systems, ensuring they are not accessible from the internet.
  • Locate control system networks and remote devices behind firewalls and isolating them from business networks.
  • When remote access is required, use more secure methods, such as Virtual Private Networks (VPNs), recognizing VPNs may have vulnerabilities and should be updated to the most current version available. Also recognize VPN is only as secure as the connected devices.

Summary

Background

  • Countries/Areas Deployed: Worldwide
  • Company Headquarters Location: Denmark

Vulnerabilities

CVE-2026-129713
A stack-based buffer overflow in an unauthenticated CGI handler of the Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA Series controller allows remote attackers to send specially crafted HTTP/S POST requests, leading to memory corruption, webserver restart and hypothetically potential arbitrary code execution with webserver privileges. Authentication is not required to exploit this vulnerability.
Read More

1 Affected Product

Danfoss AK-SM8xxA <=5.4.0

Product Status: known_affected

Remediations

Mitigation
This vulnerability will be addressed in an upcoming Danfoss AK-SM 800A Series software release (version 5.5.x). In addition, Danfoss will remove the ability for users to disable Strict Mode in future software releases.

Mitigation
Until a software update is available, Danfoss recommends the following mitigations: * Follow the guidance provided in the product documentation and do not expose devices directly to the Internet or assign them public IP addresses. * Restrict remote access to affected devices by using a secure VPN or other protected network architecture. * Configure all affected devices to operate in Strict Mode, which provides enhanced security protections. * Use strong, unique passwords for all user accounts and administrative access. * For additional security recommendations and best practices see the Danfoss AK-SM 800 security guidance page: https://www.danfoss.com/en/service-and-support/downloads/dcs/adap-kool-software/ak-sm-800a/#tab-overview

Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04: Prioritizing Security Updates Based on Risk establishes vulnerability management requirements for Federal Civilian Executive Branch (FCEB) agencies. BOD 26-04 reinforces the importance of the KEV Catalog and requires federal agencies to prioritize rapid remediation of high-risk vulnerabilities, specifically those identified by Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVEs) listed in CISA’s KEV Catalog on publicly exposed assets that grant total control of the asset post-exploitation, while deferring action for lower-risk vulnerabilities. BOD 26-04 further establishes basic expectations for when agencies must check whether threat actors compromised the system before the patch was applied.

While BOD 26-04 applies only to FCEB agencies, CISA encourages all organizations to adopt risk-based vulnerability management and prioritize remediation of KEV Catalog vulnerabilities. CISA will continue to add vulnerabilities to the catalog that meet the specified criteria.

item.title: World: 2025 IASC Gender Accountability Framework Report
item.description:
Country: World
Sources: Inter-Agency Standing Committee, UN Women

Please refer to the attached file.

UN Women and the IASC Gender Reference Group are delighted to share the 2025 IASC Gender Accountability Framework (GAF) Report.

The report provides a system-wide assessment of implementation of the 2024 IASC Policy on Gender Equality and the Empowerment of Women and Girls in Humanitarian Action. It reviews progress across gender-responsive planning and implementation; meaningful inclusion, localization and financing; Gender in Humanitarian Action (GiHA) coordination; and leadership, capacity and accountability.

The monitoring exercise covered 23 humanitarian contexts and drew on consultations with 467 participants, including UN agencies, international and national NGOs, government institutions and women-led organizations (WLOs). WLOs represented the largest share of consultation participants, at 35 per cent. The process also included 120 verified cluster survey responses across 22 countries and 10 clusters.

The global report, including detailed country snapshots, identifies progress as well as persistent gaps and challenges. Key findings include:

  • Gender analysis is increasingly informing humanitarian planning: 82 per cent of HNRPs or equivalent frameworks reflected gender analysis, up from 62 per cent in 2024. However, only 23 per cent of reporting countries had at least 75 per cent of clusters monitoring programmes for the access and inclusion of women and girls and other at-risk groups, showing that important gaps remain between analysis, implementation and monitoring.
  • WLO representation in humanitarian leadership continued to expand: 87 per cent of reporting countries confirmed WLO membership in their HCTs, up from 73 per cent in 2024. Yet representation did not always translate into influence over priorities or resource allocation. Although 83 per cent of responding clusters reported WLO membership, WLOs accounted for an average of only 15 per cent of cluster members, and six of the 16 countries with cluster Strategic Advisory Groups reported no WLO representation in those bodies.
  • WLO access to Country-Based Pooled Funds improved substantially but remained uneven: WLOs made up 21.5 per cent of direct CBPF recipients, while 18 per cent of total CBPF allocations, or $189.2 million, reached WLOs, up from 11 per cent in 2024 and above OCHA’s 15 per cent global target. However, allocations ranged from 73 per cent in Venezuela, 59 per cent in Colombia and 47 per cent in Pakistan to 1 per cent in Syria, 2 per cent in the occupied Palestinian territory and Niger, and 3 per cent in Chad and the Syria Cross-Border Humanitarian Fund.
  • GiHA Working Groups remained operational across most contexts: 87 per cent of reporting countries had a functional standalone GiHA Working Group or equivalent mechanism. WLOs represented 36 per cent of GiHA Working Group membership and co-chaired half of the active groups. However, only 58 per cent had representation from at least 75 per cent of clusters, and several groups faced possible merger or restructuring under the Humanitarian Reset, creating risks to their dedicated gender coordination and accountability functions.
  • Senior gender advisory capacity increased: 83 per cent of reporting countries had such capacity for at least nine months, compared with 64 per cent in the previous cycle. Nevertheless, only 52 per cent had gender focal points in at least 75 per cent of clusters, and funding reductions and restructuring affected the availability and effectiveness of this capacity in several contexts.
  • GBV response remained critically underfunded: Only 23 per cent of HNRP countries had at least half of their identified GBV requirements funded, while 13 of 22 response plans had less than one quarter of GBV requirements funded.

The findings also demonstrate the value of the GAF as an accountability and management tool for UN Women’s humanitarian engagement. Fourteen of the 19 countries that participated in the previous cycle reported concrete action on earlier recommendations, including stronger consultation with WLOs, expanded gender focal-point networks, reforms to pooled-fund access arrangements, and new gender strategies and funding commitments.

As the Humanitarian Reset advances amid severe funding constraints, colleagues are encouraged to use the GAF findings and country-level recommendations to inform UN Women’s engagement with humanitarian leadership, coordination bodies, clusters and partners, including through in-country GiHA Working Groups or equivalent mechanisms. Priority areas include strengthening gender-responsive planning, sustaining dedicated GiHA coordination and advisory capacity, expanding meaningful WLO influence, improving equitable access to financing, and keeping commitments to gender equality and the leadership of women and girls visible and accountable throughout humanitarian decision-making.

item.title: Brazil: Près de 20 000 personnes déplacées après une violente tempête qui a endommagé ou détruit des habitations dans le sud du Brésil
item.description:
Country: Brazil
Source: International Organization for Migration

Brasília, 24 novembre 2026 – Près de 20 000 personnes ont été déplacées après qu'une violente tempête a endommagé ou détruit 93 % des habitations dans la commune de Tupanciretã, dans le sud du Brésil, laissant des milliers de familles sans abri sûr. Au moins cinq personnes ont perdu la vie et 265 ont été blessées. L'ampleur des destructions crée des besoins immédiats en matière d'abris sûrs, d'assistance d'urgence et de soutien à la réparation ou à la reconstruction des logements.

Alors qu'environ 8 000 foyers ont été touchés et que des milliers de familles ont un besoin urgent d'abris et d'assistance, l'Organisation internationale pour les migrations (OIM) a mobilisé des équipes pour évaluer les besoins et soutenir les opérations d'intervention aux côtés des autorités locales et fédérales, notamment la Cellule de protection de l'assistance sociale du Système unifié d'assistance sociale du Brésil, ainsi que de ses partenaires.

« Nos pensées accompagnent ceux qui ont perdu des êtres chers et les milliers de familles qui ont vu leurs maisons endommagées, leurs biens détruits et leur vie bouleversée en quelques heures », a déclaré Paolo Caputo, Chef de mission de l'OIM au Brésil. « Pour beaucoup, la préoccupation immédiate est de trouver un endroit sûr pour dormir et de se procurer l'essentiel pour traverser les prochains jours. Apporter dès maintenant une assistance aux familles est déterminant pour les aider à retrouver un sentiment de sécurité et à commencer à reconstruire leur vie. »

À la suite d'une série d'épisodes météorologiques violents qui ont frappé l'État du Rio Grande do Sul depuis le 16 novembre, la dernière tempête a apporté de fortes pluies, de la grêle et des vents atteignant 114 kilomètres par heure. Selon les autorités de la Protection civile, environ 19 780 personnes ont été déplacées dans une commune qui compte à peine plus de 20 000 habitants.

Les destructions ont également gravement perturbé les services essentiels, privant les habitants d'électricité et d'eau courante dans l'immédiat. Les dommages causés à l'hôpital public ont contraint au transfert de patients vers des communes voisines, tandis que les écoles, les établissements de soins pour personnes âgées et d'autres structures résidentielles ont également été touchés. Les autorités fédérales ont depuis reconnu l'état de calamité publique dans la commune.

L'OIM a déployé une équipe à Tupanciretã le 20 novembre pour mener des évaluations des besoins, visiter un abri d'urgence et coordonner les opérations d'intervention avec les autorités locales, les représentants de la Protection civile et les partenaires humanitaires. Les premières évaluations font état de besoins urgents en matière d'abris temporaires, de réparations urgentes des habitations, d'assistance en espèces, d'articles ménagers essentiels, de soutien logistique et de services de protection pour les personnes particulièrement vulnérables.

Forte de son expérience en matière de préparation aux catastrophes et d'intervention au Brésil, notamment de ses activités en cours au Rio Grande do Sul, l'OIM mobilise son expertise technique et opérationnelle dans la gestion des abris d'urgence, la coordination humanitaire, la logistique et la distribution d'articles de secours essentiels pour appuyer les opérations d'intervention des autorités de l'État et des communes. Le rétablissement de conditions de vie sûres sera déterminant pour aider les familles à quitter progressivement les abris temporaires et à commencer à reconstruire leur vie.

Les autorités ayant mis en garde contre de nouvelles intempéries dans les prochains jours, le rétablissement d'abris sûrs et de services essentiels demeure une priorité urgente. L'OIM continue de travailler en étroite collaboration avec les autorités et les partenaires pour suivre l'évolution des besoins et soutenir à la fois l'assistance immédiate et le relèvement à plus long terme.

Afin d'accélérer l'aide aux familles qui ont perdu leur logement, leurs biens et leurs moyens de subsistance, l'OIM a uni ses forces à celles de l'Instituto Vakinha, de l'Instituto Cultural Floresta, de Humus et d'autres partenaires dans le cadre d'une campagne de collecte de fonds destinée à répondre à l'urgence.

Les fonds collectés serviront à fournir des bâches, des matériaux de toiture, des matelas, des couvertures, des kits d'hygiène et de nettoyage, des équipements de protection individuelle, de l'eau potable, des vivres et d'autres articles de secours essentiels, tout en renforçant les capacités des organisations locales et des équipes humanitaires mobilisées pour répondre à l'urgence.

Les dons destinés à soutenir les familles touchées peuvent être effectués dans le cadre de la campagne de collecte de fonds SOS RS 2026 organisée par l'Instituto Vakinha, accessible ici.

Pour plus d'informations, veuillez consulter le Centre médias de l'OIM.

item.title: Brazil: Cerca de 20.000 personas desplazadas tras una devastadora tormenta que destruyó viviendas en el sur de Brasil
item.description:
Country: Brazil
Source: International Organization for Migration

Brasilia, 24 de noviembre de 2026 – Cerca de 20.000 personas se han visto desplazadas tras una devastadora tormenta que dañó o destruyó el 93 % de las viviendas del municipio de Tupanciretã, en el sur de Brasil, dejando a miles de familias sin un lugar seguro donde alojarse. Al menos cinco personas han fallecido y 265 han resultado heridas. La magnitud de la destrucción ha generado necesidades urgentes de albergue de emergencia, asistencia humanitaria y apoyo para reparar o reconstruir las viviendas afectadas.

Con alrededor de 8.000 viviendas dañadas y miles de familias que necesitan asistencia urgente, la Organización Internacional para las Migraciones (OIM) ha movilizado equipos para evaluar las necesidades y apoyar las labores de respuesta en coordinación con las autoridades locales y federales, incluido el Grupo de Trabajo de Protección de Asistencia Social del Sistema Único de Asistencia Social de Brasil, y otros asociados.

"Nuestros pensamientos están con quienes han perdido a sus seres queridos y con las miles de familias que han visto sus hogares dañados, sus pertenencias destruidas y sus vidas trastocadas en cuestión de horas", afirmó Paolo Caputo, Jefe de Misión de la OIM en Brasil. "Para muchas personas, la preocupación inmediata es encontrar un lugar seguro donde dormir y conseguir lo indispensable para afrontar los próximos días. Hacer llegar la asistencia a las familias cuanto antes es fundamental para ayudarlas a recuperar la sensación de seguridad y comenzar a reconstruir sus vidas".

Tras una serie de fenómenos meteorológicos extremos que han afectado al estado de Rio Grande do Sul desde el 16 de noviembre, la última tormenta provocó lluvias intensas, granizo y vientos de hasta 114 kilómetros por hora. Según las autoridades de Defensa Civil, aproximadamente 19.780 personas se han visto desplazadas en un municipio de poco más de 20.000 habitantes.

La destrucción también ha provocado graves interrupciones de los servicios esenciales, dejando a los residentes sin electricidad ni agua corriente inmediatamente después de la tormenta. Los daños sufridos por el hospital público obligaron a trasladar a los pacientes a municipios vecinos. Las escuelas, los centros de atención a personas mayores y otros establecimientos residenciales también resultaron afectados. Posteriormente, las autoridades federales declararon el estado de calamidad pública en el municipio.

La OIM desplegó un equipo en Tupanciretã el 20 de noviembre para evaluar las necesidades, visitar un albergue de emergencia y coordinar la respuesta con las autoridades locales, los representantes de Defensa Civil y los asociados humanitarios. Las evaluaciones iniciales han identificado necesidades urgentes de albergue temporal, reparaciones de emergencia en las viviendas, asistencia en efectivo, artículos domésticos esenciales, apoyo logístico y servicios de protección para las personas en situación de especial vulnerabilidad.

Sobre la base de su experiencia en preparación y respuesta ante desastres en todo Brasil, incluida su labor en curso en Rio Grande do Sul, la OIM está movilizando sus capacidades técnicas y operativas en materia de gestión de albergues de emergencia, coordinación humanitaria, logística y distribución de suministros esenciales para apoyar las labores de respuesta de las autoridades estatales y municipales. Restablecer condiciones de vida seguras será fundamental para ayudar a las familias a dejar atrás los albergues temporales y comenzar a reconstruir sus vidas.

Ante las advertencias de las autoridades sobre posibles nuevos fenómenos meteorológicos extremos en los próximos días, garantizar el acceso a albergues seguros y restablecer los servicios esenciales siguen siendo prioridades urgentes. La OIM continúa trabajando estrechamente con las autoridades y los asociados humanitarios para dar seguimiento a las necesidades que vayan surgiendo y apoyar tanto la asistencia inmediata como la recuperación a largo plazo.

Para contribuir a acelerar la asistencia a las familias que han perdido sus hogares, pertenencias y medios de vida, la OIM ha unido fuerzas con el Instituto Vakinha, el Instituto Cultural Floresta, Humus y otros asociados en una campaña de recaudación de fondos de emergencia.

Los fondos recaudados se destinarán al suministro de lonas, materiales para la reparación de techos, colchones, mantas, kits de higiene y limpieza, equipos de protección personal, agua potable, alimentos y otros suministros esenciales. También contribuirán a fortalecer la capacidad de las organizaciones locales y los equipos humanitarios que participan en la respuesta a la emergencia.

Las donaciones para apoyar a las familias afectadas pueden realizarse a través de la campaña de recaudación de fondos SOS RS 2026, organizada por el Instituto Vakinha.

Para más información, visite el Centro de Prensa de la OIM.
